Raymond Stauffer: 
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. As you are all aware, this is my first 
earnings call as the CEO of Nazara. Well, since day one, my priority has been to align the teams 
and operations while leveling up group capabilities by enhancing Nazara’s central platform. And 
part of that has started to show throughout Q2 FY27. This quarter, as you’ve seen, has been a 
key step in Nazara’s evolution into a global gaming platform. It is also the first quarter to include 
Bluetile and BestPlay, consolidated from 1 August 2026. 
Q2 was a record quarter for us: Revenue was INR 803 crores, our highest ever, up 53% year-on-
year. EBITDA grew 93% to INR 120 crores and EBITDA margin expanded 311 basis points to 
14.9%. Profit After Tax from continuing operations was INR 35 crores, compared with a loss of 
INR 34 crores in Q2 FY26. For H1 FY27: Revenue grew 20% to INR 1,232 crores and EBITDA 
grew 52% to INR 166 crores. 
Gaming revenue grew 122% to INR 656 crores at a 21.5% EBITDA margin, contributing 82% 
of consolidated revenue and effectively all EBITDA before corporate costs. 
Mobile revenue grew 167% to INR 550 crores. In their first two months as part of Nazara, 
Bluetile and BestPlay generated revenue of INR 329 crores, up 49%. EBITDA grew 64% to INR 
64 crores, driven by rapid product iterations, new markets, AI-automated user acquisition, and 
cross-promotion. Bluetile’s leadership team holds 5.8% of Nazara, aligning our interests 
effectively with all of our shareholders. Our existing gaming studios delivered organic growth 
of 11% in revenue and 17% in EBITDA, underpinned by sustained investment in content. 
WildWorks grew revenue 41% on Animal Jam content. Kiddopia grew revenue by 21% and 
Fusebox launched The Traitors and a new Big Brother season. 
Curve grew revenue about 27% and EBITDA 61%, driven by Sovereign Tower, the mobile debut 
of Wobbly Life, and Human: Fall Flat, which has surpassed 60 million players.
